heroIntro: For Non-Resident Bangladeshis (NRBs) residing in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, or Australia, managing ancestral land, selling real estate, executing development agreements, or representing family interests in court without physically travelling to Bangladesh requires a legally unimpeachable Power of Attorney (আমমোক্তারনামা). Under the Power of Attorney Act 2012 (পাওয়ার অব অ্যাটর্নি আইন, ২০১২) and the Power of Attorney Rules 2015, any instrument executed outside Bangladesh is subject to a rigorous, non-negotiable three-tier authentication regime: Consular attestation abroad, Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) verification in Dhaka, and stamp duty adjudication by the District Collector (DC Office). A single procedural error—such as an incomplete property schedule, missing photograph seals, or missing statutory deadlines under the Stamp Act 1899—renders the deed void ab initio, unregistrable at the Sub-Registry, and legally inadmissible in Bangladeshi civil courts. This comprehensive guide walks expatriate landowners through the exact legal framework, drafting requirements, embassy workflows, domestic stamping protocols, and revocation mechanisms.

quickAnswer.heading: Power of Attorney from Abroad: The Complete Procedural Checklist
points: Draft the deed strictly following the statutory format of Form 1 under the Power of Attorney Rules 2015.
Schedule an appointment and appear in person before a Consular Officer at the Bangladesh Embassy or High Commission in Washington DC, New York, London, Toronto, etc.
Sign the deed before the Consular Officer; both Principal and Attorney photographs must be affixed and stamped across with the official mission seal.
Dispatch the original attested deed to Bangladesh via secure courier (DHL/FedEx) to the nominated Attorney or legal counsel.
Submit the deed to the Consular & Welfare Wing of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA), Segunbagicha, Dhaka within 4 months of arrival.
Present the MOFA-authenticated deed to the Collector (Deputy Commissioner / DC Office) under Section 18 of the Stamp Act 1899 for stamp duty adjudication and embossing.
If the power involves property transfer or sale, register the adjudicated deed at the competent Sub-Registry Office under the Registration Act 1908.

sections.h2: 1. Statutory Framework: Power of Attorney Act 2012 & 2015 Rules
sections.content:
Executing an overseas Power of Attorney is strictly governed by Section 6 of the Power of Attorney Act, 2012 (Act No. 35 of 2012) read with Rule 13 of the Power of Attorney Rules, 2015. Prior to the 2012 Act, fraudulent powers of attorney executed on plain paper or via informal notary endorsements caused rampant land litigation across Bangladesh. The 2012 legislative overhaul established unambiguous statutory safeguards to protect both absent landowners and third-party buyers.

Key statutory provisions that every Non-Resident Bangladeshi must understand include:

  • Section 6(1) of the 2012 Act: Mandates that any Power of Attorney executed outside Bangladesh must be executed before an authorized officer of the Bangladesh Foreign Mission stationed in that foreign country.
  • Rule 13(1) of the 2015 Rules: Prescribes that the deed must strictly adopt Form 1 of the Schedule. Any substantive omission of statutory declarations renders the document invalid.
  • Section 18 of the Stamp Act, 1899: Stipulates that every instrument executed out of Bangladesh chargeable with duty must be stamped by the Collector within three months (extended to four months in administrative practice) after it has been first received in Bangladesh.
  • Sections 17 and 33 of the Registration Act, 1908: Dictate when a Power of Attorney must be compulsorily registered before a Sub-Registrar to confer legal capacity to convey title or execute sale deeds.

Without full compliance across all four statutes, the document cannot be presented in any court of law, land revenue office (AC Land), or Sub-Registry in Bangladesh.

sections.h2: 2. Three Types of Powers: General, Special, and Irrevocable
sections.content:
Expatriates must exercise utmost legal precision when selecting the nature of the power granted. Confusing these categories can result in an untrustworthy agent selling off ancestral assets without permission:

A. Special Power of Attorney (নির্দিষ্ট আমমোক্তারনামা)

A Special Power of Attorney confers limited, explicitly demarcated authority for a designated legal act. Examples include:

  • Filing or defending a specific partition suit (বাটোয়ারা মামলা) or title suit in a Civil Court.
  • Applying for e-Mutation (ই-নামজারি) and paying Land Development Tax before the Assistant Commissioner (Land).
  • Applying for certified copies of Khatians (CS, SA, RS, BS) and Registered Deeds from the Sub-Registry.
  • Overseeing building renovations or collecting commercial rents.

Once the specified purpose is fulfilled, the authority automatically extinguishes. This is the safest, most recommended instrument for expatriates managing family land affairs from abroad.

B. General Power of Attorney (সাধারণ আমমোক্তারনামা)

Under Section 2(1) of the 2012 Act, a General Power confers comprehensive administrative powers over all properties or multiple assets of the Principal. While an agent holding a General Power can sign lease agreements, supervise caretakers, and pay municipal taxes, a General Power does NOT automatically authorize the agent to sell, gift, mortgage, or execute a registered transfer deed unless express, unambiguous language granting power of alienation is explicitly written into the deed and registered at the Sub-Registry.

C. Irrevocable Power of Attorney for Land Transfer (অপ্রত্যাহারযোগ্য পাওয়ার অব অ্যাটর্নি)

Under Section 2(2) and Section 6 of the 2012 Act, an Irrevocable Power of Attorney is an instrument executed in connection with a contract for sale (বায়না চুক্তি), financial consideration, or a real estate joint-venture development agreement with a developer. Key attributes:

  • It cannot be cancelled or revoked unilaterally by the Principal without court intervention or mutual registered deed.
  • It requires mandatory registration at the competent Sub-Registry office upon arrival in Bangladesh.
  • If the Principal dies, the power does not automatically lapse; the legal heirs remain bound by the obligations under Section 14 of the 2012 Act.

sections.h2: 4. Step 1 — Drafting the Deed in Statutory Form 1
sections.content:
A Power of Attorney drafted in colloquial English or relying on standard Western notary templates will be outright rejected by Bangladeshi revenue authorities. Under Rule 13 of the Power of Attorney Rules 2015, the draft must strictly incorporate Form 1. Drafting should be carried out by an advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh or experienced land counsel.

Mandatory drafting components include:

  1. Principal's Identification: Full name, Bangladeshi Passport Number (or foreign passport with NVR endorsement), Overseas Residential Address, Permanent Address in Bangladesh, Father's and Mother's names.
  2. Attorney's Identification: Full name, Bangladeshi National ID (NID) number (mandatory), Father's and Mother's names, permanent address, and active telephone/email.
  3. Exhaustive Property Schedule (তফসিল):
    • District, Sub-Registry Office, Police Station (Thana), and Union/Ward.
    • Mouza name and JL Number.
    • Khatian Numbers: CS, SA, RS, and City Survey / BS (as applicable).
    • Dag / Plot Numbers: CS, SA, RS, and BS.
    • Exact area of land in Acres, Decimals (শতাংশ), or Square Feet, along with physical boundaries (চৌহদ্দি: North, South, East, West).
  4. Specific Operative Clauses: Itemized list of authorized actions. Avoid general blanket statements like 'to do all lawful acts'; specify whether the agent can sign plaints, appear before the AC Land, compromise disputes, receive money, or execute sale deeds.
  5. Affidavit of Execution: The statutory declaration confirming that the Principal is executing the instrument voluntarily, of sound mind, and without undue influence.

sections.h2: 5. Step 2 — Consular Signing & Attestation at Bangladesh Missions Abroad
sections.content:
Once the deed is drafted, the Principal must personally attend the diplomatic mission having territorial consular jurisdiction over their residence.

Mandatory Procedure at the Embassy or High Commission:

  1. Personal Appearance: Under Section 6(1) of the Act, all Principals granting the power must appear physically. Postal or mail-in signing without personal appearance is prohibited.
  2. Photographs: Affix passport-sized color photographs of both the Principal and the nominated Attorney at the designated locations on the first page of the deed.
  3. Signature in Consular Presence: The Principal must sign every page of the deed and append their signature/thumb impression in the direct presence of the Consular Officer.
  4. Cross-Stamping: The Consular Officer signs and places the official metal embossed seal and rubber stamp partly across the photograph and partly across the page. This prevents fraudulent photo substitution.
  5. Consular Fee Receipt: Obtain the official consular fee receipt and keep a scanned digital backup of the attested deed before physical dispatch.

sections.h2: 7. Step 3 — Verification at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) in Dhaka
sections.content:
Following embassy attestation abroad, the original document must be dispatched to Bangladesh via secure courier (DHL or FedEx). Under Bangladeshi law, consular signatures abroad are not automatically judicially recognized until endorsed by the central executive government.

Section 18 Limitation Warning: The deed must be presented to the Consular and Welfare Wing of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA), 1st Building, Segunbagicha, Dhaka within 4 months of its physical receipt in Bangladesh. Failure to submit within statutory limitation requires a cumbersome condonation application accompanied by postal tracking proofs.

MOFA Authentication Protocol:

  • The attorney or their engaged advocate submits the original deed at the MOFA Consular Counter between 9:30 AM and 12:30 PM on government working days.
  • MOFA officials match the embassy seal and signature against the official Diplomatic Signature Registry maintained by the Ministry.
  • Upon authentication, MOFA places an official barcode sticker, endorsement stamp, and authorized signature on the reverse of the deed.
  • Standard turnaround time is 24 to 48 hours with zero government fee.

sections.h2: 8. Step 4 — Adjudication of Stamp Duty by the District Collector (DC Office)
sections.content:
Under Section 18 read with Sections 31 and 32 of the Stamp Act, 1899, every instrument executed outside Bangladesh chargeable with stamp duty must be adjudicated and validated by the Collector (Deputy Commissioner / DC Office) of the district where the property is situated or where the attorney resides.

The DC Office Adjudication Procedure:

  1. Filing the Adjudication Petition: The attorney submits a formal petition under Section 31 to the Treasury / Revenue Branch of the DC Office, attaching the MOFA-endorsed deed, property Khatians, and NID copies.
  2. Assessment of Duty: The Collector assesses the appropriate stamp duty under Schedule I of the Stamp Act:
    • Special Power of Attorney: Fixed stamp duty ranging from BDT 500 to BDT 1,000 depending on the nature of court or administrative representation.
    • General Power for Management: BDT 1,000 to BDT 2,000 fixed stamp duty.
    • Power Authorizing Land Sale: Ad-valorem stamp duty or statutory fixed stamp duty (typically BDT 2,000 to BDT 5,000 depending on jurisdiction).
  3. Deposit via Treasury Chalan: The duty is deposited through an official Treasury Chalan (ট্রেজারি চালান - Code 1-1101-0025-2681) at Bangladesh Bank or designated branches of Sonali Bank.
  4. Collector's Certificate & Embossing: The Collector endorses a formal Certificate of Adjudication under Section 32 on the deed and affixes an embossed seal, certifying that full stamp duty has been collected.

sections.h2: 9. Step 5 — Registration at the Sub-Registry Office
sections.content:
Is registration at the Sub-Registry mandatory for all overseas powers? This depends strictly on the legal objective of the document:

  • When Registration is NOT Required: A Special Power of Attorney authorizing an attorney to represent the NRB in a civil lawsuit (partition suit, recovery suit) or handle administrative mutation before the AC Land does NOT require Sub-Registry registration once DC Office adjudication is complete. The DC-embossed deed is immediately valid and acceptable in all civil courts under Section 85 of the Evidence Act 1872.
  • When Registration IS Mandatory: Under Section 6 of the Power of Attorney Act 2012 read with Section 17 of the Registration Act 1908, any Power of Attorney that authorizes the attorney to execute, register, or convey a deed of transfer (sale, gift, mortgage, or lease exceeding one year) MUST be registered at the Sub-Registry Office having local jurisdiction over the land within 4 months of DC office adjudication.

sections.h2: 10. Fatal Drafting & Procedural Defects That Cause Rejection
sections.content:
Attorneys at Advocate Md. Shah Alam Chamber routinely encounter invalid overseas deeds executed by expatriates without professional guidance. The most common fatal mistakes include:

  • Vague or Incomplete Property Schedule: Stating 'My 10 decimals land in Uttara, Dhaka' without specifying Mouza, JL Number, CS/SA/RS/BS Khatian numbers, and Dag numbers. Sub-Registrars will summarily refuse registration.
  • Signing Before a Foreign Public Notary: An attestation by a US Notary Public, UK Solicitor, or Canadian Commissioner of Oaths has zero validity under Section 6 of the 2012 Act. The deed MUST be executed before a Bangladeshi Consular Officer.
  • Missing Photo Seal Across Face: If the consular officer signs below the photo instead of stamping across the photograph and the paper, the DC office will reject the document on suspicion of photo substitution.
  • Expiration of the 4-Month Window: Allowing more than 4 months to elapse between arrival in Bangladesh and submission to MOFA or DC Office without formal legal condonation.
  • Conflict of Interest: Appointing an attorney who is simultaneously the prospective buyer in a contract for sale without express disclosure.

sections.h2: 11. Real-World Case Study: NRB Land Sale from New York to Dhaka
sections.content:
Background: Mr. Tariq Ahmed, a permanent resident of Queens, New York, inherited an undivided 6-decimal residential plot in Uttara Sector 11, Dhaka following his father's demise. A local developer offered BDT 2.5 Crore for the plot. Mr. Tariq could not travel to Bangladesh due to his employment.

Legal Strategy Implemented:

  1. Our chamber drafted a customized Special Power of Attorney in statutory Form 1, conferring specific authority to his elder brother in Dhaka to sign the development agreement, apply for RAJUK plan clearance, and receive consideration through account-payee banking channels.
  2. Mr. Tariq attended the Consulate General of Bangladesh in New York with his valid Bangladeshi passport and NID, executing the deed before the Consular Officer.
  3. The attested deed was dispatched to Dhaka via DHL. Our team completed MOFA authentication at Segunbagicha within 48 hours.
  4. We submitted the adjudication petition to the Dhaka Deputy Commissioner's Revenue branch, paid the statutory treasury chalan duty, and secured the Collector's embossing.
  5. The deed was presented to the Uttara Sub-Registry Office for formal registration under Section 17. The entire transaction was concluded safely in 24 business days without Mr. Tariq booking a single flight.

sections.h2: 12. Legal Procedure for Revoking an Overseas Power of Attorney
sections.content:
If an expatriate discovers that their appointed attorney is acting against their financial interests, attempting unauthorized encumbrances, or misrepresenting rental proceeds, the power can be extinguished immediately:

  1. Draft a Deed of Revocation (আমমোক্তারনামা বাতিল দলিল): Must conform to Form 4 of the Power of Attorney Rules 2015, stating the original deed number, date, and reasons for cancellation.
  2. Consular Execution Abroad: The Principal executes the cancellation deed before the Bangladesh Embassy or High Commission abroad following the identical authentication procedure.
  3. Service of Formal Legal Notice: An enrolled Supreme Court advocate serves a formal Legal Notice under Section 11 of the 2012 Act to the Attorney via registered post with A/D, immediately terminating all legal agency.
  4. Notification to Authorities: Formal intimation copies are dispatched to the Sub-Registrar, Assistant Commissioner (Land), and relevant Civil Courts.
  5. Public Notice in National Dailies: Publish a formal notice of revocation in one Bengali national daily (e.g. Daily Ittefaq/Prothom Alo) and one English national daily (e.g. The Daily Star) to notify the public and invalidate third-party dealings.

faqs.question: Can I execute a Power of Attorney if my Bangladeshi Passport has expired?
faqs.answer: Yes. If your Bangladeshi passport is expired, you can present your foreign passport (US, UK, Canadian) provided it carries a valid 'No Visa Required' (NVR) seal or you produce your original 10-digit/17-digit Bangladeshi National ID (NID) card or Dual Nationality Certificate.

faqs.question: Can I execute a Power of Attorney for property sale without going to the Embassy?
faqs.answer: No. Under Section 6 of the Power of Attorney Act 2012, personal appearance before a Consular Officer of the Bangladesh Mission abroad is mandatory. Remote notary or digital execution is invalid under Bangladeshi real estate law.

faqs.question: What is the penalty if an Attorney misuses their power or sells land illegally?
faqs.answer: Under Section 13 of the Power of Attorney Act 2012 and Section 406/420 of the Penal Code 1860, fraudulent misuse of power of attorney is punishable with rigorous imprisonment up to 5 years, along with separate criminal liability under the Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023.

faqs.question: How long does the entire Power of Attorney process take from USA/UK to Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Consular attestation abroad takes 2 to 5 working days. International courier takes 3 to 4 days. MOFA authentication in Dhaka takes 2 days, and DC office adjudication takes 7 to 15 business days. The complete cycle takes approximately 3 to 4 weeks.

faqs.question: Does a Power of Attorney remain valid after the death of the Principal?
faqs.answer: A Special or General Power of Attorney automatically terminates upon the death of the Principal. However, under Section 14 of the 2012 Act, an Irrevocable Power of Attorney executed for consideration survives and binds the legal heirs.

faqs.question: Can I appoint two Attorneys simultaneously to act jointly or severally?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can appoint multiple attorneys in Form 1, specifying whether they must act jointly (যৌথভাবে - both must sign all documents) or severally (পৃথকভাবে - either attorney can act independently).

faqs.question: Can a foreign national spouse be appointed as an Attorney for Bangladesh land?
faqs.answer: While legally permissible, it is highly impractical. The Attorney must physically attend land revenue offices, sub-registries, and courts in Bangladesh. Appointing a Bangladeshi citizen resident in Bangladesh with a valid NID is strongly advised.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss the 4-month limitation deadline for MOFA or DC office stamping?
faqs.answer: Your advocate must file a formal application under Section 18 of the Stamp Act 1899 showing 'sufficient cause' (such as medical emergency or postal delay) accompanied by courier receipts to secure condonation of delay from the Collector.
